units.quote: The farmers reported 24, 20 and 6% chances of crop failure due to aberrant rains in crop + livestock, crop + livestock + tree and crop + livestock + tree + farm pond rainfed farming systems, respectively during the rainy season.

relationship.outcome_raw: farmer-reported chance of rainy-season crop failure from aberrant rain, farm pond + crop + tree + livestock vs crop + tree + livestock (lower = more stable)

context.note: Research Square preprint of the Agroforestry Systems paper; on-farm survey of 85 farmers in 2021 comparing system types (only 11 with a farm pond); farm pond bundled with trees and livestock

units.question: Preprint; 11 farmers with ponds. Keep as low-tier evidence or reject?

units.citation: Palsaniya et al. (2023). Rain water harvesting, agroforestry and goat based intensification for livelihood resilience in drought prone rainfed smallholder farming system: a case for semi-arid tropics. Agroforestry Systems.
units.quote: During the winter season, 100% chances of crop failure were reported by farmers in crop + livestock and crop + livestock + tree based farming systems. They further observed that the chances of crop failure due to aberrant rainfall during the winter season reduced to 5–10% if farmers had a farm pond for rain water harvesting and recycling.

relationship.outcome_raw: farmer-reported chance of winter (dry-season) crop failure with vs without a farm pond (value_with = upper end of the stated range)

context.note: Research Square preprint of the Agroforestry Systems paper; on-farm survey of 85 farmers in 2021 comparing system types (only 11 with a farm pond); farm pond bundled with trees and livestock; dry-season cropping made possible by stored water (supplemental irrigation), not buffering of a drought event - no hazard tag

units.question: Dry-season result is really irrigation from the pond, not rainfed buffering — right variable / practice?

units.citation: Mazvimavi et al. (2009). Socioeconomic and institutional factors influencing adoption of conservation farming by vulnerable households in Zimbabwe. Agricultural Systems.
units.quote: Farmers adopting CF for the ﬁrst time or those with experience (second + year) achieved higher maize grain yields than those practicing conventional farm practices in the 2006/07 crop- ping season, even with the use of chemical fertilizer (Table 6). First-year practitioners obtained an average maize yield of 1520 kg ha1, compared to 368 kg ha1 of maize grain realized from their conventionally managed plots, with no fertilizer appli- cation. Where fertilizer was applied to conventional farm practice, the control, yield gains were marginally higher, but not adequate to compare with CF plots. Therefore, yield gains achieved with CF practices represented close to 300% increase, in a season consid- ered a drought year for Zimbabwe (FAO, 2007).

relationship.outcome_raw: maize yield, first-year planting-basin CF vs conventional plots without fertiliser, in a season considered a drought year

context.note: hand-hoe conservation farming = dry-season planting basins (zai-type in-situ harvesting) + manure + micro-dosed N + residue; NGO-supported vulnerable households, 2006/07; CF package includes topdressing N absent from the no-fertiliser control (bundled effect); values match the low-rainfall (450-650 mm) row of the sensitivity table

units.question: Drought-year yield gain of conservation farming is confounded with fertiliser and manure.

units.citation: Abasse et al. (2023). Farmer managed natural regeneration in Niger: the state of knowledge. .
units.quote: FMNR has a positive impact on agricultural yields, but what is the situation in a drought year? In 2011 Niger recorded a large cereal deficit due to drought. Yamba and Sambo (2012) conducted a study in two departments in the Zinder Region (Kantché and Mirriah) with very high population densities, but also with high FMNR densities. One of the conclusions was that these departments produced a cereal surplus in 2011. The department of Kantché even had a surplus of almost 13,000 tonnes.

relationship.outcome_raw: departments with high FMNR tree density produced a cereal surplus in a drought year (national cereal deficit)

context.note: department-level co-occurrence, not a with/without contrast; high population density confound

units.question: Departments with dense FMNR had a cereal surplus in a drought year — co-occurrence across departments, confounded by population density. Evidence or not?

units.citation: Bayala et al. (2014). Parklands for buffering climate risk and sustaining agricultural production in the Sahel of West Africa. Current Opinion in Environmental Sustainability.
units.quote: Cereal (C4 plant) grain yield difference was found to be varying from 0.54 t ha1 under Balanites aegyptiaca to +0.24 t ha1 under F. albida and biomass yield difference from 1.31 t ha1 under P. biglobosa to +4.07 t ha1 under Prosopis africana. Legumes (cowpea and groundnut) seem to be less affected by tree cover while tuber (Colocasia esculenta) yield is rather improved under trees compared to the treeless monoculture plot of the same crop (+0.40 to +1.67 t ha1). Both legumes and tubers are C3 plants expected to show greater shade tolerance than the C4 plants. Patterns for cereals are in line with the meta- analysis results of Bayala et al. [13]. The observed yield reductions for cereals have been attributed to competition for light, nutrients and water

relationship.outcome_raw: cereal grain yield in the influence zone of parkland trees vs treeless control: from a loss under Balanites to a small gain under Faidherbia, mostly reduced

context.note: direction is the modal cereal response; legumes less affected and tubers improved under trees (same quote)

units.question: Cereal yield under parkland trees coded NEGATIVE from a range that runs from a loss under one species to a gain under another.

units.citation: Cisneros-Saguilán et al. (2024). Sistemas silvopastoriles, una alternativa para atenuar el impacto del cambio climático en la ganadería. Idesia (Arica).
units.quote: Asimismo, en Colombia fue posible incrementar el nivel de carga animal a 4.3 vacas ha-1 y la produc- ción de leche al 130 %, además de eliminar comple- tamente el uso de fertilizantes químicos, al emplear un SSP compuesto de pastos, árboles de tamaño grande y medio y arbustos de Leucaena. También en las épocas de sequía intensa se mantuvo cons- tante la producción de forraje y se pudo neutralizar los efectos negativos en todo el sistema silvopasto- ril, al compararse con el monocultivo de gramíneas, en el que se redujo la biomasa al 25 % (Altieri y Nicholls, 2013). (English: Likewise, in Colombia it was possible to raise stocking to 4.3 cows ha-1 and milk production to 130%, while completely eliminating chemical fertilisers, using a silvopastoral system of pastures, large and medium trees and Leucaena shrubs. Also, in periods of intense drought forage production stayed constant and the negative effects on the whole silvopastoral system could be neutralised, compared with grass monoculture, in which biomass was reduced to 25% (Altieri and Nicholls, 2013).)

relationship.outcome_raw: stocking rate and milk output raised with a Leucaena-based silvopastoral system while chemical fertiliser was eliminated

context.note: narrative review, Idesia (Arica) 2024

units.quote: Betancourt et ál. (2003) mencionan que la producción de leche de animales bajo sistemas con alta densidad de árboles se incrementó en 29% en comparación con animales que pastoreaban potreros con baja cobertura arbórea, los autores lo atribuyen a la reducción en el es- trés calórico y a la mayor cantidad de follaje y frutos en los primeros potreros, en otros trabajos se encontraron incrementos superiores a 15% en producción de leche en animales que se pastoreaban en sistemas silvopasto- riles, comparado con animales que estuvieron a pleno sol (Souza et ál., 2000). relationship.outcome_raw: milk production of cows grazing high tree-density pasture vs low tree-cover pasture, attributed to lower heat stress and more foliage and fruit
